messages:
marie: :rotating_light: Incoming — multiple support tickets and 5xx/401 spikes hitting the auth tier since 14:40 UTC. Appears correlated with this morning's SSO refresh rollout window. Getting a lot of "failed refresh" errors and client retries.

ajay: seeing the same in dashboards — spike in error rate on /v1/auth/refresh and a concurrent increase in Redis timeouts. Latency from auth nodes to redis jumped around the same time as leader-election churn.

sylvia: support queue is full. Customer-facing symptom: new API calls failing with 401 and errors like `invalid_token` or `refresh_failed`. Some customers report billing hooks failing too.

marie: reproducible locally against staging? Need quick repro steps so support can triage.

ajay: repro steps I used:
```bash
# simulate heavy refresh traffic
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"sso_provider":"corp-sso","refresh_token":"fake-${i}"}' \
    https://auth.internal.redwood/v1/auth/refresh &\
 done
wait
```
You see many `503` from auth despite upstream SSO being healthy. Logs show retry storms and backpressure.

marie: any config flips today? I remember we scheduled smaller refresh concurrency defaults for the rollout.

tim: we did toggle the `SSO_REFRESH_BATCH_SIZE` and enabled a leader-election tweak to speed up failover (k8s leader-elect). The leader-election change seems to have caused rapid leader churn on some nodes in us-west-2 — that increases cache misses and sends more refresh requests to SSO provider.

rachel: support-bot: Affected customers: #2345, #2348, #2359. All filed between 14:42–14:55 UTC. Escalated to enterprise.

marie: immediate mitigation options? Ideas: revert leader-election change, raise token TTL for affected tenants, or enable a short-term in-memory local cache to prevent full refresh on every request.

ajay: quick and safest: roll back the leader-election flag first. Doing that will stop the churn and allow KV cache warm-ups. I can roll back via `kubectl set env deployment/auth-service LEADER_ELECTION_INTERVAL=5s` -> back to 30s.

sylvia: can we throttle refresh calls at the gateway to avoid hitting the SSO and auth backend? A per-tenant rate limit for refresh should reduce storms.

marie: agree. Deploy-bot, can you confirm current canary state and whether we can safely rollback leader-election config to previous value?

deploy-bot: canary status: auth-service v2.14.3 rolled to 10% in us-west-2 at 14:20 UTC. No deployment in progress. Flag `LEADER_ELECTION_INTERVAL` set to `5s` (changed at 14:15 UTC).

ajay: I'm going to patch canary to set `LEADER_ELECTION_INTERVAL=30s` and scale the canary to 0 temporarily. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: patch applied to "auth-service-canary". New env var `LEADER_ELECTION_INTERVAL=30s` set at 14:58 UTC. Scaling canary -> 0 at 14:59 UTC.

marie: monitor metrics. If errors drop, we can proceed to full rollback.

(2m later)

ajay: error rate on /v1/auth/refresh dropped ~70% in canary region, redis timeouts falling. Customer 401 incidents reduced.

rachel: support-bot: Notified escalated customers that we're rolling back a config change; suggested workaround: retry after 2 minutes. They acknowledged.

tim: one more note: we discovered a bug in the refresh path where a failed kv lookup caused immediate external refresh attempts instead of exponential backoff. Combined with leader churn this created a retry storm. Patch queued.

marie: what's the short-term patch?

ajay: add a jitter+backoff on cache-miss-triggered refreshes and fallback to previous valid token if present. Patch branch `hotfix/auth-refresh-backoff` created. Requesting an emergency approval for quick deploy.

sylvia: QA: please include a regression test that simulates leader churn and ensures we don't exceed X refresh/sec per tenant.

marie: support please keep customers updated. Tim — can you coordinate emergency deploy? I want it to target canary first, then roll to full region if green.

tim: on it. ETA 25m for canary deploy. I'll run the following kubectl patch as part of the rollout:
```bash
kubectl set env deployment/auth-service AUTH_REFRESH_BACKOFF_ENABLED=true -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service -n prod
```
I'll also increase per-node request queue from 200 -> 400 to absorb a bit more burst until code fix lands.

(Deploy bot)

deploy-bot: emergency canary deploy started at 15:20 UTC — auth-service hotfix v2.14.4-canary.

(10m later)

ajay: canary looks stable: 2k requests with <1% error on refresh path, redis latency normalized. Rolling to remaining hosts now.

deploy-bot: rollout complete at 15:36 UTC. auth-service v2.14.4 live in all regions.

marie: can we do a quick checklist for post-incident:
- confirm root cause: leader-election interval change + missing backoff on cache miss -> retry storm -> redis saturation -> 5xx/401s
- mitigation: rollback leader-election change + deploy backoff hotfix + temporary per-node queue increase
- customer impact: ~17 enterprise tenants saw transient 401s and webhook failures between 14:40–15:15 UTC
- follow-ups: add regression tests, add dashboard for refresh/sec per-tenant, and review rollout gating for leader-election flags

rachel: support-bot: Notified all affected customers with timeline and ETA for postmortem.

sylvia: I'll own the postmortem doc. Will include logs, graph snapshots, and hipchat timeline.

marie: thanks everyone. Please keep thread updated with any delayed customer reports. We'll schedule a 1hr postmortem tomorrow 09:00 PST. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Incident closed for now — monitoring continues for 2h.

marie: adding notes to the incident tracker and tagging oncall for follow-up.

tim: small follow-up: we should add a safety throttle in the gateway that limits refresh attempts per session to 3 per minute; I'll open a PR.

ajay: PR #4892 opened: `gateway: per-session refresh throttle`. Link: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/4892

marie: good. End of thread.
